result.summary: Checked lib/letflow/design/iss0279-issue-closure-audit.md against CODE-DESIGNER's own 6 acceptance criteria from handoffs/WF03-ISS0279-20260822/step-02-code-designer.json, per-criterion verdict: AC1 (design doc exists, covers both fix surfaces) PASS -- SS1 (doc prose) and SS2 (Mix.Task) both present. AC3 (Mix.Task design complete: @moduledoc, CLI shape, gh command(s) and JSON fields, grandfather-list format matching lint_handoffs's convention, exit-code/report format) PASS WITH A NOTED STRUCTURAL DEVIATION -- see grandfather-list finding below; all other sub-elements (exact @moduledoc prose S2.2, zero-arg CLI shape S2.3, exact `gh issue view --json number,state,comments,closedByPullRequestsReferences` call and field list S2.4, exit-code/report format S2.7) are fully specified. AC5 (letflow.check-wiring question resolved with rationale addressing network risk) PASS -- S2.1 Q2 resolved as NO, with rationale directly addressing the alias-breaking risk (spurious fail in sandboxed/offline runs) and an explicit rejection of a graceful-skip variant. AC6 (no implementation code) FAIL -- see below. GRANDFATHER-LIST FORMAT vs lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex's real convention (read in full, lines 133-176): lint_handoffs uses a 2-tuple {rule, path} list plus a separate defp grandfathered?/2 that does exact-tuple membership; dates/traceability live only in surrounding comments, not in the tuple itself. The design's S2.5 uses a 3-tuple {issue_number, date, note} -- a genuine structural difference from the real precedent, not an identical mirror. The design explicitly acknowledges and justifies the deviation (single hard rule here vs. lint_handoffs's several, so a `rule` slot would be redundant, and folding date/note into the tuple keeps per-item dating inline rather than in comments) -- the underlying convention it must match (per-item exact grandfathering, no wildcards/ranges, individually dated and traced, reported-but-non-failing) is preserved, so this is a documented, reasoned adaptation rather than a sloppy mismatch. Flagging per the validator's own task brief, but not treated as fail-worthy on its own. IMPLEMENTATION CODE FOUND (fails AC6 and the validator's own 'no implementation code' gate criterion, which the design text itself claims to satisfy): S2.5 contains a complete, working one-line function body, not a bare signature -- `@spec grandfathered?(integer()) :: boolean()` followed by `defp grandfathered?(number), do: Enum.any?(@grandfathered, fn {n, _, _} -> n == number end)`. This is real, correct, pasteable Elixir logic (a pattern-matched Enum.any? call), not a type shape or interface description -- it crosses the same line the design's own S2.5 sentence ('per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own gate criteria... no implementation code') says it must not cross. WF-02 Step 1b's rule is fail-immediately-and-completely on any single failed check, no partial credit -- this one function body is sufficient by itself to FAIL the gate even though every other criterion passed cleanly.
